contracts.boundary: Real native Pi AgentSession dispatch through the production extension with a hard routingScope: a real Auto turn dispatches only the permitted provider, the excluded provider is never called or reached over the network, in both exclude directions, and an empty allowlist dispatches no provider at all. Scope is an eligibility filter applied first in resolveHealthyModel; it never dispatches on its own.
contracts.assertions: Shared native faux harness: the fenced in-process faux run dispatches the permitted provider with an exact per-provider call count and zero excluded-provider calls in both directions; deny-all dispatches nothing. Unit evidence: scope runs before economic admission, reliability, affinity, and strategy selection; a scoped fallback uses the fallback tier's allowlist while the global allowlist stays request-wide; exclusions report reason provider_not_allowed with the global or tier origin. Compilation fails closed on absent, empty, partially malformed, duplicated, and unknown-field allowlists; the composition helper intersects layers so a later source can only narrow and reports disjoint nonempty allowlists as conflicts.

contracts.boundary: An optional schema-version-2 routingScope in layered Bifrost configuration: global and per-tier exact provider allowlists validate through the shared config validator on both the Pi path and the Router SDK snapshot path, intersect across config layers so a later source only narrows, and first-use setup preserves an explicit scope without inventing one.
contracts.assertions: Config validation requires schemaVersion 2, rejects unknown fields, malformed or duplicated providers, and unknown tiers by stable code and path, and reports a tier allowlist that cannot intersect the global allowlist as a strict config error that blocks routing. Layer loading intersects provider allowlists and diagnoses a disjoint override; source-local diagnostics reject an invalid scope with the shared unknown-tier gate. The shipped schema gates routingScope behind schemaVersion 2 and keeps allowlists exact; init/serialize keeps an existing routingScope and drops malformed entries.
